title: Removing something from the eye
what: With numbing drops, the doctor finds and gently removes the particle from your eye. It usually takes a few minutes.
why: When dust, a metal chip, or another particle gets into your eye and will not wash out.
tell_doctor: What got into your eye and when
If you were working with metal, a grinder, or wood
If you are allergic to any eye drops

prepare.title: Do not rub
prepare.text: Do not rub your eye. It can scratch the cornea.

prepare.title: Rinsing
prepare.text: You can rinse your eye with clean water. Do not try to remove the particle with anything sharp.

prepare.title: Contact lenses
prepare.text: If you have a lens in, take it out with clean hands if you can.

bring: Your glasses, if you wear them
Someone to go with you, if you cannot see well
steps: The doctor puts in numbing drops
The eye is checked under a microscope
Sometimes a dye is used to see scratches
The particle is removed with a moist swab or a fine tool
If a rust mark is left, it is removed too
Medicated drops or ointment are put in
feel: After the drops, it barely hurts
When the drops wear off, it may feel like sand in the eye and sting
The eye may water and be sensitive to light for a day or two
after: Use drops or ointment as the doctor said
Do not rub your eye or wear contact lenses until you are allowed
If needed, come back for a check the next day
Wear safety glasses when working with metal
red_flags: Pain does not go away or gets worse after a day
Pus or a white spot on the eye
If a fast-flying fragment hit the eye, see a doctor right away. Call emergency services if the injury is severe

faq.q: Why shouldn't I rub my eye?
faq.a: The particle can scratch the cornea and go deeper.

faq.q: Should I see a doctor if it seems to have washed out?
faq.a: Yes, if it still feels like something is there, the eye is red, or you see worse.

reminders.text: Do not rub your eye. If it still feels like something is in it, see an eye doctor.
